args.slovnik.terminy.TZB.popis: A collective term for HVAC, heating, cooling, sanitary installations, gas, and measurement and control — everything that distributes heat, cold, air, and water in a building.
args.slovnik.terminy.VZT.popis: A system that supplies fresh air to a building, extracts stale air, and along the way filters, heats, or cools it.
args.slovnik.terminy.ZTI.popis: Water supply, drainage, and fixtures in a building.
args.slovnik.terminy.MaR.popis: Sensors, controllers, and a control system that maintain set values — temperature, humidity, flow rate — without human intervention.
args.slovnik.terminy.BMS.popis: A supervisory system for the building. It collects data from all systems, monitors alarms, and allows operation to be managed from a single point.
args.slovnik.terminy.PENB.full: energy performance certificate of a building
args.slovnik.terminy.PENB.popis: A mandatory document assessing the energy performance of a building. It is prepared by an energy specialist and registered in the ENEX database.
args.slovnik.terminy.ENEX.popis: A registry of certificates, audits, and assessments managed by the Ministry of Industry and Trade.
args.slovnik.terminy.MPO.popis: The central authority responsible for energy legislation and the ENEX database.
args.slovnik.terminy.BIM.popis: A design approach where instead of drawing lines you model real elements with properties. From the model you can extract schedules, clash detection, and documentation for building management.
args.slovnik.terminy.TČ.popis: A device that transfers heat from outdoor air, the ground, or water into the heating system. For every kilowatt-hour of electricity it delivers several kilowatt-hours of heat.
args.slovnik.terminy.EAC.popis: A filter that charges dust particles and captures them on collector plates. Compared to a conventional filter cartridge, it has a lower pressure drop and can be washed.
args.slovnik.terminy.AHU.popis: The mechanical heart of ventilation: fans, filters, heat exchangers, and heat recovery in a single cabinet. In English, air handling unit.
args.slovnik.terminy.ZZT.popis: Recovery. Outgoing warm air transfers its heat to incoming fresh air — without the two streams mixing.
args.slovnik.terminy.PM2,5.popis: Particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres. They penetrate deep into the lungs, which is why the purpose of filtration is to capture precisely these.
args.slovnik.terminy.TVOC.popis: A collective indicator of gaseous organic compounds in indoor air — from furniture, adhesives, paints, and cleaning products. Measured when assessing indoor air quality.
args.slovnik.terminy.KJ.popis: A device that produces electricity and heat simultaneously. Fuel utilisation is significantly higher than with electricity generation alone.
args.slovnik.terminy.PBŘ.popis: Part of the documentation specifying fire resistance, escape routes, and the behaviour of ventilation systems in the event of a fire.
args.slovnik.terminy.TNS.popis: A vessel operating under pressure for which regulations require periodic inspections — typically expansion vessels and storage tanks.
args.slovnik.terminy.COP.popis: The ratio of heat delivered to electricity consumed at a given moment. A COP of 4 means four kilowatt-hours of heat for every one kilowatt-hour of electricity.
args.slovnik.terminy.SCOP.popis: Heating coefficient averaged over an entire heating season. A fairer metric than COP for comparing heat pumps.
args.slovnik.terminy.EER.popis: The ratio of cooling capacity to electrical power consumed.
args.slovnik.terminy.VRF.popis: Air conditioning system in which a single outdoor unit serves multiple indoor units, with refrigerant flow controlled according to the actual demand of each unit.
args.slovnik.terminy.DSP.popis: Design stage used by the building authority to assess the construction project.
args.slovnik.terminy.DPS.popis: Detailed design stage used as the basis for actual on-site installation.
args.slovnik.terminy.RDS.popis: Documentation prepared by the contractor for its own execution, building upon the construction execution documentation.
args.slovnik.terminy.TDS.popis: A specialist representing the investor's interests on site — monitors quality, scope, and compliance with the design.
args.slovnik.terminy.ČSN.popis: National technical standard. Specifies requirements such as fresh air volume, noise levels, or equipment safety.
args.slovnik.terminy.HVAC.popis: English abbreviation for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning. The international equivalent of the Czech term TZB.

out.slovnik.stranka.lead: In our industry, few people go easy on abbreviations. Here they are explained — and wherever you come across one on the site, just hover over or tap it.
out.slovnik.stranka.hledat: Search for an abbreviation or term
out.slovnik.stranka.nenalezeno: We don't have that abbreviation yet. Ask us.
out.slovnik.terminy.TZB.popis: A collective term for HVAC, heating, cooling, sanitary installations, gas, and measurement and control — everything that distributes heat, cold, air, and water in a building.
out.slovnik.terminy.VZT.popis: A system that supplies fresh air to a building, extracts stale air, and along the way filters, heats, or cools it.
out.slovnik.terminy.ZTI.popis: Water supply, drainage, and fixtures in a building.
out.slovnik.terminy.MaR.popis: Sensors, controllers, and a control system that maintain set values — temperature, humidity, flow rate — without human intervention.
out.slovnik.terminy.BMS.popis: A supervisory system for the building. It collects data from all systems, monitors alarms, and allows operation to be managed from a single point.
out.slovnik.terminy.PENB.full: energy performance certificate of a building
out.slovnik.terminy.PENB.popis: A mandatory document assessing the energy performance of a building. It is prepared by an energy specialist and registered in the ENEX database.
out.slovnik.terminy.ENEX.popis: A registry of certificates, audits, and assessments managed by the Ministry of Industry and Trade.
out.slovnik.terminy.MPO.popis: The central authority responsible for energy legislation and the ENEX database.
out.slovnik.terminy.BIM.popis: A design approach where instead of drawing lines you model real elements with properties. From the model you can extract schedules, clash detection, and documentation for building management.
out.slovnik.terminy.TČ.popis: A device that transfers heat from outdoor air, the ground, or water into the heating system. For every kilowatt-hour of electricity it delivers several kilowatt-hours of heat.
out.slovnik.terminy.EAC.popis: A filter that charges dust particles and captures them on collector plates. Compared to a conventional filter cartridge, it has a lower pressure drop and can be washed.
out.slovnik.terminy.AHU.popis: The mechanical heart of ventilation: fans, filters, heat exchangers, and heat recovery in a single cabinet. In English, air handling unit.
out.slovnik.terminy.ZZT.popis: Recovery. Outgoing warm air transfers its heat to incoming fresh air — without the two streams mixing.
out.slovnik.terminy.PM2,5.popis: Particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres. They penetrate deep into the lungs, which is why the purpose of filtration is to capture precisely these.
out.slovnik.terminy.TVOC.popis: A collective indicator of gaseous organic compounds in indoor air — from furniture, adhesives, paints, and cleaning products. Measured when assessing indoor air quality.
out.slovnik.terminy.KJ.popis: A device that produces electricity and heat simultaneously. Fuel utilisation is significantly higher than with electricity generation alone.
out.slovnik.terminy.PBŘ.popis: Part of the documentation specifying fire resistance, escape routes, and the behaviour of ventilation systems in the event of a fire.
out.slovnik.terminy.TNS.popis: A vessel operating under pressure for which regulations require periodic inspections — typically expansion vessels and storage tanks.
out.slovnik.terminy.COP.popis: The ratio of heat delivered to electricity consumed at a given moment. A COP of 4 means four kilowatt-hours of heat for every one kilowatt-hour of electricity.
out.slovnik.terminy.SCOP.popis: Heating coefficient averaged over an entire heating season. A fairer metric than COP for comparing heat pumps.
out.slovnik.terminy.EER.popis: The ratio of cooling capacity to electrical power consumed.
out.slovnik.terminy.VRF.popis: Air conditioning system in which a single outdoor unit serves multiple indoor units, with refrigerant flow controlled according to the actual demand of each unit.
out.slovnik.terminy.DSP.popis: Design stage used by the building authority to assess the construction project.
out.slovnik.terminy.DPS.popis: Detailed design stage used as the basis for actual on-site installation.
out.slovnik.terminy.RDS.popis: Documentation prepared by the contractor for its own execution, building upon the construction execution documentation.
out.slovnik.terminy.TDS.popis: A specialist representing the investor's interests on site — monitors quality, scope, and compliance with the design.
out.slovnik.terminy.ČSN.popis: National technical standard. Specifies requirements such as fresh air volume, noise levels, or equipment safety.
out.slovnik.terminy.HVAC.popis: English abbreviation for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning. The international equivalent of the Czech term TZB.
